In a vacuum, there are two point charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ located at points A and B on a horizontal straight line, respectively. The distance between the two points is $r = 30 \, \text{cm}$, with $q_1 = -1.0 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{C}$ and $q_2 = +1.0 \times 10^{-9} \, \text{C}$. The electrostatic force constant is given as $k = 9.0 \times 10^9 \, \text{N·m}^2/\text{C}^2$.

1. Find the force exerted by $q_2$ on $q_1$ at point A.
2. Find the field strength at point A.
3. The electric field strength at point A after removing $q_1$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$1 \times 10^{-8} N$, direction horizontally to the left
100N/C, direction horizontally to the right
100N/C

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the two points are on the same horizontal straight line, point B is on the left, labeled q2; point A is on the right, labeled q1. Therefore q2 is located to the left of q1. Reasoning: It is known that r = 30 cm = 0.30 m, q1 = -1.0×10^-10 C, q2 = +1.0×10^-9 C, k = 9.0×10^9 N·m^2/C^2. By Coulomb's law, the magnitude of the force of q2 on q1 is F = k|q1 q2|/r^2 = (9.0×10^9 × 1.0×10^-10 × 1.0×10^-9)/(0.30)^2 = 1.0×10^-8 N. Since q1 and q2 have opposite signs and attract each other, and q2 is on the left and q1 is on the right, the direction of the force on q1 is horizontally to the left. The electric field strength at point A corresponding to this force satisfies the vector relationship F = q1 E. Because q1 is a negative charge, the direction of the electric field is opposite to the direction of the force on q1, that is, horizontally to the right. The magnitude of the electric field strength is E = F/|q1| = (1.0×10^-8)/(1.0×10^-10) = 100 N/C. After removing q1, the electric field at point A is the field produced by the source charge q2, and does not depend on whether q1 exists, so the magnitude and direction do not change, still 100 N/C, directed horizontally to the right.

raw_record.original_question:
In a vacuum, there are two point charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ located at points A and B on a horizontal straight line, respectively. The distance between the two points is $r = 30 \, \text{cm}$, with $q_1 = -1.0 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{C}$ and $q_2 = +1.0 \times 10^{-9} \, \text{C}$. The electrostatic force constant is given as $k = 9.0 \times 10^9 \, \text{N·m}^2/\text{C}^2$.

1. Find the force exerted by $q_2$ on $q_1$ at point A.
2. Find the field strength at point A.
3. The electric field strength at point A after removing $q_1$.
raw_record.answer:
$1 \times 10^{-8} N$, direction horizontally to the left
100N/C, direction horizontally to the right
100N/C
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the two points are on the same horizontal straight line, point B is on the left, labeled q2; point A is on the right, labeled q1. Therefore q2 is located to the left of q1.

Reasoning: It is known that r = 30 cm = 0.30 m, q1 = -1.0×10^-10 C, q2 = +1.0×10^-9 C, k = 9.0×10^9 N·m^2/C^2. By Coulomb's law, the magnitude of the force of q2 on q1 is F = k|q1 q2|/r^2 = (9.0×10^9 × 1.0×10^-10 × 1.0×10^-9)/(0.30)^2 = 1.0×10^-8 N. Since q1 and q2 have opposite signs and attract each other, and q2 is on the left and q1 is on the right, the direction of the force on q1 is horizontally to the left.

The electric field strength at point A corresponding to this force satisfies the vector relationship F = q1 E. Because q1 is a negative charge, the direction of the electric field is opposite to the direction of the force on q1, that is, horizontally to the right. The magnitude of the electric field strength is E = F/|q1| = (1.0×10^-8)/(1.0×10^-10) = 100 N/C.

After removing q1, the electric field at point A is the field produced by the source charge q2, and does not depend on whether q1 exists, so the magnitude and direction do not change, still 100 N/C, directed horizontally to the right.
